name: UCLA

preview.title: UCLA, decoded on one page
preview.description: What UCLA says matters most, where admitted students landed, and 4 moves to make before Nov 30. Straight from UCLA's own Common Data Set.
preview.image_line: Only 3 things are top-tier. Test scores count for zero.
preview.share_text: UCLA's one-page application cheat sheet, straight from UCLA's own data.

library.blurb: Only 3 things are top-tier. About 1 in 11 got in.

hero.sub: Straight from UCLA's own 2025–26 Common Data Set.

chances.title: About 1 in 11 applicants got in.

lede.s: 145,086 students applied for fall 2025. 13,659 got in. Most of them had great grades, so the rest of this page is about where you can still stand out.
lede.p: 145,086 students applied for fall 2025. 13,659 got in. Most of them had great grades, so the rest of this page is about where your student can still stand out.

grids.aria: About 9 of 100 dots filled: 9.4% of first-year applicants were admitted

chances.src: Fall 2025 first-years (C1): 13,659 of 145,086 admitted (9.4%). UCLA's Common Data Set doesn't split this by California vs. out of state.

ladder.title: Only 3 things are top-tier. Test scores aren't considered at all.
ladder.lede: By senior fall, your classes and GPA are mostly set. Your essays, which UC calls Personal Insight Questions (PIQs), are the top-tier piece you can still change before Nov 30.
considered: First in your family to go to college
not_considered: How often you toured or emailed
ladder.note: Top tier = where your hours go before Nov 30 ↓
ladder.src: Section C7, first-year admission factors, 2025–26 Common Data Set.

numbers.lede: Type your GPA on a 4.0 scale to see where it sits next to UCLA's first-years. This is a range, not a cutoff.

gpa.default: Average GPA of enrolled first-years: 3.94 on a 4.0 scale.
gpa.near: Right around UCLA's average. Now your top-tier rows decide it: how hard your classes were, and your PIQs.
gpa.above: At or above UCLA's average. Good start. Your classes and PIQs still do the heavy lifting.
gpa.below: Below UCLA's average. That's not a no. Your PIQs are top-tier too, and they're the piece you can still change. Put your hours there.

facts.text: of enrolled first-years had a 4.0 GPA. Another 35% were between 3.75 and 3.99.

numbers.src: Sections C11–C12: enrolled first-years, fall 2025 (99.8% reported a GPA). UCLA doesn't use SAT/ACT scores or class rank in admission (C7, C8).

dates.title: One deadline. No early round at UCLA.

items.html: UC application due. One application covers every UC campus.

dates.src: UC application deadline (admission.universityofcalifornia.edu), checked Nov 4, 2026. Decision and reply dates: Section C, 2025–26 Common Data Set.

kicker.s: Send this part to your parents

money.title: If you qualify for aid, UCLA meets about 91% of need on average.
money.lede: The sticker price isn't your price. The net price calculator gives your family a real estimate in about 15 minutes.
money.aid_line: About 4 in 10 first-years get need-based grants. The average need-based package is $34,312 a year.
money.src: Sections G1 and H2, 2025–26 Common Data Set. Tuition and required fees only; on-campus housing and food (about $19,779) cost extra.

title.s: Are your PIQs doing their job?
title.p: Are your student's PIQs doing their job?

lede.s: PIQs are top-tier at UCLA. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read all 4 of your PIQs together, then tap what's true.
lede.p: PIQs are top-tier at UCLA. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read all 4 of your student's PIQs together, then tap what's true.

items.title: Each one answers the exact question asked.
items.body: Circle the key words in the question. Every paragraph should answer them, not a question close to them.

items.title: Only you could have written it.
items.body: Swap in a friend's name. If it still works, it isn't specific enough yet.

items.title: It shows what you did.
items.body: Your role, your steps, what changed. Not just what the team or club did.

items.title: The 4 show 4 different sides of you.
items.body: If two PIQs tell the same story, swap one for a side of you the reader hasn't met yet.

after.s: Not sure you can check all four? That's normal. It's hard to judge your own writing.
after.p: Not sure? That's normal. It's hard to judge writing you're close to.

self_check.all_done: All 4. Nice work. A fresh reader can still catch what you can't see.

take.heading: What I saw as an admissions reader
take.quote: When almost everyone has a 3.75 or higher, grades stop telling readers apart. Your PIQs are where a reader finally meets you. Give them four different reasons to remember you.

title.s: Want a former admissions reader to read your 4 PIQs?
title.p: Want a former admissions reader to read your student's 4 PIQs?

lede.s: I read applications at UChicago. I'll read all 4 of your PIQs together the way a reader would and rank what to fix first. You do the writing. I give the feedback. One read covers every UC you apply to.
lede.p: I read applications at UChicago. I'll read all 4 of your student's PIQs together the way a reader would and rank what to fix first. Feedback only, so the writing stays theirs. One read covers every UC they apply to.
